requirements.summary: Executor installed /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance with '15 2 * * * root /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1', verified present and syntactically correct, confirmed cron service active, and confirmed the cron.d file persisted with identical content after a full reboot.

Log file created with correct permissions; a functional run of the exact cron command line appended output (stdout+stderr) to the log both before and after the restart, and prior content was preserved across the restart, demonstrating durable append-only retention.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (cf34dc87...) and healthy state (cron active, cron.d content, log content) captured; reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnection; node was unreachable during the transition (timeout on cmd-f81eb2a0c8784b7e) then returned with a different boot_id (9b2870e1...), independently corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity snapshots; post-restart state showed cron active/enabled, cron.d persisted, script executable, log persisted, and a fresh functional re-run appended new output.

overall_summary: The executor correctly scheduled /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance via /etc/cron.d for 02:15 daily with output appended to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log, verified this functionally, and completed a full, well-evidenced restart cycle (pre-restart baseline, acknowledged reboot, unreachability, new boot_id, and full post-restart recovery of cron, script, and log). No unnecessary or unsafe mutations were found; the only anomaly (a malformed heredoc artifact left in the target script's content) predates the executor's work and is outside the task's scope of fixing the script itself.
limitations: The target script /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance appears to contain a broken heredoc artifact (a literal 'SCRIPT' line and leftover provisioning commands), causing 'SCRIPT: not found' errors on every run; this predates the executor's actions (matches the prepare-stage baseline hash) and the task only required scheduling/log retention, not fixing script content, so it was not scored as a task failure, but it does mean the retained log output includes an error rather than clean success output.

Boot-identity change is corroborated by both executor commands and fixed global snapshots, but no independent evidence beyond boot_id (e.g., dmesg or kernel uptime) was captured to further rule out anomalies; this is a minor evidentiary gap.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map to legitimate purposes: chmod 755 on the script restored the execute bit needed for cron to run it (prerequisite), chmod 644 and creation of the cron.d file and log file are the core deliverable, the functional test runs (cmd-ec524eb0cf194b6e, cmd-b36e02f85e094bb6) are bounded verification appends to the target log itself (not unrelated residue), and the reboot (cmd-330c4dae4ef4496d) is the mandated restart protocol. No abandoned files, failed services, unnecessary exposure, or package-state damage appear in the after_executor snapshot versus after_prepare (only boot-identity, ephemeral systemd-private /tmp dirs, and socket PIDs changed, all expected reboot side effects). One caveat: the script content shown (containing a literal 'SCRIPT' heredoc artifact and provisioning lines) appears to be a pre-existing preparation-stage defect, not something the executor introduced or was asked to fix, so it is not counted against hygiene.
